PG1.quote: require `pagy/extras/limit` and rename the settings ... Fixing only the require is not enough. I tested that variant ... The old `DEFAULT` keys are silently ignored, so pagy 9's own defaults apply: 20 per page, the `?limit=` parameter, and a cap of 100 ... Use `@pagy.limit` there.
PG1.reasons: Applicability: the plan says the silent drift came from the require-only variant, but in that variant the view fails on `@pagy.items`; drift appears only once the require and the reader are both fixed. Validation: the plan checks page 2 at size 5 (6-10), the 500→50 cap, the last page and that filters stay in the links, but leaves out following the real Next href to 11-15, default 10, size 25, the owned/foreign data controls, /journal, empty search, the foreign 404 and the anonymous redirect.

PG2.quote: Malformed page numbers now raise ... bad values raise an error and the request fails with a 500 ... def pagy_get_page(*) page = super; page.is_a?(Integer) ? [page, 1].max : page ... It also works on 8.6.3, so it can go out first
PG2.reasons: Validation: the invalid inputs are tested with a single note and judged mostly by HTTP status, not compared to page-one content, and there are no valid next-page, filtering or ownership controls (only the existing test and a stale last-page control).
